q8.answer: Each count lives in the shared Redis store under the key rl:{customerId}:{windowStart}, so all six gateway instances read and increment the same number. The first increment sets EXPIRE to 120 seconds, so each key outlives its 60-second window and Redis deletes it on its own; no cleanup job is needed.

q9.answer: A customer's budget resets at each UTC minute boundary, because the next window computes a new windowStart and therefore a new, empty key. The old key is removed by its 120-second expiry. There is no other recovery path.

q10.answer: The check and increment run as one Lua script in Redis, which Redis executes as a single atomic unit, so no other command can run between the GET and the INCR. Two gateways cannot both read the same count below the limit and both increment past it.

q11.answer: The gateway computes Retry-After as ceil(windowStart + 60 - now) in whole seconds, using its own clock at the moment it denies the request. The Lua script returns only the allowed flag and the count, so time is not handled in the store. A denied request always falls inside a live window, so the value is at least 1.

q12.answer: The design does not specify a retry of the counter store. Each request makes its own store call with the 50 ms timeout, and the design excludes a circuit breaker, so the next request tries the store again. The client gets the backend's response with no X-RateLimit-Limit or X-RateLimit-Remaining headers, and the gateway's only signal is the internal ratelimit_store_unavailable metric. Clients are told a missing header is not an error.
